1) the provision of ecosystem service bundles in rice agroecosystems will change under climate and land-use drivers; and 2) land-use changes may partially offset the effects of climate change, but at the expense of other services.
climate and land-use scenarios have opposing effects on the provision of essential ecosystem services in rice croplands.

climate and land-use scenarios have a strong impact on the provision of a range of ecosystem services, and that the interactions between ecosystem services have to be taken into account when assessing the effects of global change on the provision and management of ecosystem services.

the question: How can we manage rice agro-eco-systems to maintain their ability to provide multiple ecosystem services (ESS) in the face of global climate and land-use dynamics?
the question of how to manage the trade-offs between ESS in rice agroecosystems in the future, and which ESS should be prioritised in order to ensure food security and other ESS.
the effects of climate change on the provision ecosystem services (ESS) and the interaction between E SS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
land-use changes may partially compensate climate change impacts in the short-term, but that the provision of ESS is likely to be negatively affected by climate and land-use in the long-term.

climate change will have a strong negative impact on ESS, and that the negative impacts of climate change on ESS can be partially compensated by land-use change, but that this compensation comes with the loss of natural ecosystems.
the provision of all services in the study areas will be affected by climate and land-use scenarios in the future, but the magnitude of the changes depends on the specific scenario.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate change and land use change are the two major drivers for the future provision of ecosystem services, especially the food provision.

the combined effects of climate and agricultural land-use change on ecosystem services in irrigated rice croplands in the Philippines and in Vietnam are complex and depend on the region and the specific land-use and climate scenarios.
we need a more holistic view on the interactions of climate change, land use change and the provision of ecosystem goods and services.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combined effects of climate and agricultural land-use change on ESS provision can be positive or negative, depending on the specific region and the type of service considered.
the combined effect of climate and land use change on the provision ESS in rice agroecosystems is more complex and less straightforward than the effects of each driver alone.

the combined effects of climate and socio-economic change on the provision ESS in rice agroecosystems can be substantial and that the trade-offs between different ESS have to considered when designing sustainable land-use and management strategies.
